paper_summary: Tensile behaviour of syntactic foams made by injection moulding expandable PMMA-shell polymer microballoons (Expancel 950-120, ~120 um) into two PP/SEBS 70/30 blends (SEBS A = small 80-140 nm particles, SEBS B = large 200-250 nm particles) at 0-50 vol% microballoon, i.e. relative densities 0.5-1.0, tested at nominal strain rates of 1, 10 and 100 1/s. Apparent elastic modulus rises with strain rate (a drastic rise between 10 and 100 1/s, delayed by adding microballoons) while yield stress rises only slightly; ductility collapses as soon as any microballoons are added. PP/SEBS A foam moduli follow the Gibson-Ashby rho^2 law at 10 and 100 1/s whereas PP/SEBS B foams fall well below it, and both foams reach similar moduli regardless of matrix modulus.

the nominal strain rates were 1, 10 and 100 s-1 in the PP/SEBS syntactic foams because of the limited number of syntactic foam specimens. Apparent elastic modulus, yield stress and strain energy up to failure were measured

The microballoon was Expancel grade 950 ~120 (Akzo Nobel) whose average diameter was about 120 um. The material of microballoon's shell was made of polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA). The average thickness of the microballoon's shell was about 0.1 um
The tensile mechanical properties of PP/SEBS blend syntactic foams with the relative densities from 0.5 to 1.0 are characterized at the nominal strain rates of 1, 10 and 100 s-1.

extraction_notes: NO numeric property values could be extracted. Every mechanical result in this paper (apparent elastic modulus, yield stress, strain energy to failure, Gibson-Ashby and rule-of-mixtures comparisons) is presented only in Figs. 2-8, 11 and 12; the paper states no modulus, strength, strain or density number in the running text. Table 1 (SEBS grades) and Table 2 (foam compositions) are present in the PDF but their cells came through the text extraction empty ([TABLE p2-1] contains only captions), so nothing could be read from them. Per rule 2 all Properties fields are therefore null and no values were read off the plots. Records enumerate the (composition x strain rate) grid that was actually tested: 2 matrices x 9 microballoon volume fractions (0, 2, 4, 8, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 vol%) x 3 nominal strain rates (1, 10, 100 1/s) = 54 records. The 0 vol% rows are the neat PP/SEBS matrix baselines (the neat blends were actually swept over 0.3-100 1/s; only the three rates shared with the foams are recorded). Relative density is given in microstructure_notes rather than measured_density_g_cc because the paper never states an absolute density in g/cm3; relative density = 1 - microballoon volume fraction, which the paper itself confirms (2 vol% -> 0.98, and it discusses 0.9 and 0.8 foams). matrix_class = 'pp' for the PP/SEBS 70/30 blends (PP is the 70 vol% majority phase; the SEBS is part of the matrix blend, not a filler, so additional_fillers is null). particle_wall_thickness_ratio left null: the paper gives a ~0.1 um shell thickness on a ~120 um mean diameter but never reports a radius ratio, so no eta was derived. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 200 C is the injection nozzle temperature (mould 40 C, injection pressure 75 MPa). Test temperature not stated, left null.
